_comment: globalConcurrencyLimit bounds children WITHIN one batch. It does NOT bound how wide a `runs.all` fan-out may open, which upstream also states in its own docs; keep a fan-out inside the provider's concurrency budget in the `concurrency` map of config/routing.json yourself. `parallel.maxTasks` and `parallel.concurrency` are dormant as of pi-subagents 0.57.0 — their resolvers are never called — and are kept set so a later release finds a conservative value already here. A run also carries a cumulative child budget, maxSubagentSpawnsPerRun, default 64 and live unset. See docs/adr/0005-unbounded-fan-out-on-runs-all.md. || Two spawn budgets are set here, 20 each. maxSubagentSpawnsPerRun 20 is BELOW the package default of 64 and is CUMULATIVE over one run tree with claims never released or refunded (pi-subagents docs/configuration.md:262), so it is a total-spawn budget, not a width cap: a long multi-wave research run can exhaust it part-way through and be refused its next child. Size it against the widest workflow you actually run before lowering it further. maxActiveAsyncRunsPerSession 20 replaces UNLIMITED, not a default of 4 - unset or 0 keeps unlimited behaviour (docs/configuration.md:272); it bounds concurrently active top-level async runs and does NOT bound runs.all fan-out, since workflow children do not reserve a slot. || maxSubagentSpawnsPerSession is deliberately NOT set, and the omission is a decision (2026-08-27) rather than an oversight. The rule applied was: cap it if it bounds simultaneity, leave it unlimited if it is a session total. It is a session total - it counts every child launched in one parent session including the completed and the failed ones (pi-subagents docs/configuration.md:252), and its counter has no release path - so setting it would cap how much work one session may do in total, not how much it does at once. maxActiveAsyncRunsPerSession above is the concurrency-shaped key and is already 20. Do not add the session key expecting it to bound width.
